claim_labels.claim: Dry cord care standard for facility births
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence

claim_labels.claim: CHX indication limited to high-mortality home-birth settings or replacing harmful substances
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence

claim_labels.claim: Nigerian practice prevalence data (spirit 89%, hot compress 25%, toothpaste 9%)
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence

claim_labels.claim: Jos RCT non-inferiority of methylated spirit
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence
claim_labels.source: Shwe et al. Niger J Clin Pract 2021 PMID 34018987 (Jos RCT)

claim_labels.claim: Omphalitis red-flag set and sepsis progression risk
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence

claim_labels.claim: Clean, dry cord care is WHO's recommendation for facility births and low neonatal-mortality settings
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence

claim_labels.claim: Daily 7.1% chlorhexidine application is recommended only for HOME births in high neonatal-mortality settings (>30/1000), or to replace harmful traditional substances
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence

claim_labels.claim: Umbilical stump normally separates within roughly 5-15 days; separation after 3 weeks warrants medical review
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence

claim_labels.claim: Methylated spirit was non-inferior to 4% chlorhexidine gel for preventing omphalitis in a randomized trial in Jos, Nigeria (323 mother-baby pairs)
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence
claim_labels.source: Shwe et al. Niger J Clin Pract 2021 PMID 34018987 (Jos RCT)

claim_labels.claim: Common applied substances in Nigerian practice include toothpaste (8.9%) and hot compresses (24.8%); hot compresses and herbal pastes are the documented dangers, not spirit alone
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence
claim_labels.source: Onubogu et al. Asian J Pediatr Res 2022 (Nnewi practice survey)

claim_labels.claim: Omphalitis red flags are spreading periumbilical redness, purulent/foul discharge, swelling/hardening, fever >=38C or temperature instability, poor feeding/lethargy; any sign needs same-day medical care
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence

claim_labels.claim: Omphalitis can progress to sepsis rapidly; newborns may show hypothermia instead of fever
claim_labels.label: sourced_evidence
